title.rendered: Best Daily Devotionals Around the World to Read in 2026: Our Top Recommendations

excerpt.rendered: Our editor-picked list of the best daily devotionals around the world to read in 2026, including Gospelbuzz’s own The Gospel For Today, Our Daily Bread, Open Heavens, Rhapsody of Realities and more.

content.rendered:
If you have ever set out to grow your walk with God in a more consistent way, you already know the secret weapon: a good daily devotional. A few quiet minutes each morning, a Scripture, a short reflection, a prayer, can shape a whole day, and over time, a whole life. The question most readers wrestle with is not whether to read one, but which of the best daily devotionals in the world to commit to.

At Gospelbuzz, we read a lot of them. So we put together this carefully curated list of the best daily devotionals around the world, the ones we recommend to our community, the ones our editors quietly rely on, and yes, the one we publish here every morning. Whether you are brand new to quiet time, a busy parent grabbing five minutes before the school run, a youth leader looking for material to share, or a seasoned believer searching for fresh fire, there is something on this list for you.

How We Chose the Best Daily Devotionals

We did not just pick the most popular titles. We looked for best daily devotionals that are theologically faithful, widely accessible (most are free online or via app), translated for global readers, and proven over time, some go back more than a century, others are brand new for 2026. We also made a point to include strong Nigerian and African voices alongside Western classics, because the global Church is global, and our readers deserve a list of best daily devotionals that reflects that.

We are featuring our own The Gospel For Today devotional first, because it is the one we know inside out. After that, the list is loosely ordered by global reach and historical influence, not personal ranking. Every devotional below earned its place.

1. The Gospel For Today: Gospelbuzz Daily Devotional

Publisher: Gospelbuzz · Where to read: Free on the Gospelbuzz Devotional section

The Gospel For Today is the daily devotional we publish here at Gospelbuzz, fresh every morning at 6:00 AM. Each entry centres on a single passage of Scripture, recently we have walked our readers through Psalm 1, Proverbs 4, Philippians 4, Romans 12, Colossians 3 and more, and pairs the text with a short, accessible reflection that lands the truth in everyday life. We deliberately keep entries short enough to read in five minutes and rich enough to chew on all day.

What makes it distinct? Three things. First, it is unapologetically Christ-centred: every reflection points back to Jesus and the gospel. Second, it is written with a global Christian audience in mind, especially African readers, while drawing on the broad treasure of the historic Church. Third, it is free, link-friendly and shareable, which makes it perfect for WhatsApp groups, family devotions and small-group leaders. Our Weekly Devotional Roundup also collects the week’s entries in one easy read for anyone who missed a day.

Best for: Anyone who wants a short, faithful daily Scripture meditation in clear modern English, and readers who already enjoy Gospelbuzz’s wider gospel news and music coverage.

2. Our Daily Bread

Publisher: Our Daily Bread Ministries · Founded: 1956 (ministry roots to 1938)

Few devotionals are as quietly influential as Our Daily Bread. Started by the De Haan family out of a small radio Bible class in Grand Rapids, Michigan, the booklet is now distributed in over 150 countries and more than 50 languages, reaching tens of millions of readers each year. Each daily entry pairs a Scripture, a real-life story or illustration, and a closing thought or prayer. It is gentle, accessible and theologically careful, an excellent starter devotional and an enduring favourite for seasoned believers.

Best for: New believers, families, and anyone who wants warm, story-driven Bible reflections.

3. My Utmost for His Highest: Oswald Chambers

Publisher: utmost.org · Compiled: 1927, from Oswald Chambers’ teaching

If Our Daily Bread is the warm cup of tea, My Utmost for His Highest is the strong black coffee. Compiled by his wife Biddy after his death, Oswald Chambers’ classic is famous for its piercing, almost surgical call to surrender. Many of its lines have become household quotations among serious Christians for over 90 years. The language is older and the reflections demanding, but the spiritual reward is immense.

Best for: Readers ready to be challenged at the level of motive, surrender and discipleship.

4. Open Heavens: Pastor E. A. Adeboye

Publisher: Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG) · Read online: RCCG Live Open Heavens

For millions of Nigerian and African Christians, the day does not begin properly without Open Heavens. Written by Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, General Overseer of the RCCG, each entry includes a memory verse, a Bible reading, a short message, action point and prayer point. It is practical, prayerful and deeply Pentecostal, with a strong emphasis on holiness, hearing God and walking in His promises. It remains one of the most read daily devotionals in Africa.

Best for: African Christians, Pentecostal and charismatic readers, and anyone who wants a clear “do this today” takeaway.

5. Rhapsody of Realities: Pastor Chris Oyakhilome

Publisher: rhapsodyofrealities.org · Founded: 2001

Often called the “Messenger Angel”, Rhapsody of Realities has been translated into more than 8,000 languages and dialects and distributed in over 240 countries, making it one of the most translated daily devotionals on earth. Written by Pastor Chris Oyakhilome of Christ Embassy / LoveWorld, each entry features a theme scripture, a teaching, a daily confession and a one-year Bible reading plan. The tone is bold, faith-filled and confession-based.

Best for: Readers who love faith-confession teaching, Word-of-Faith tradition, and an aggressive missions-minded posture.

6. DCLM Daily Manna: Pastor W. F. Kumuyi

Publisher: Deeper Christian Life Ministry · Since: 1996

Written by Pastor William F. Kumuyi, founder of the Deeper Christian Life Ministry (DCLM), Daily Manna is a staple in households and churches across Nigeria and the African diaspora. It is famously direct, scripture-saturated, and unwavering in its emphasis on holiness, repentance and Christian character. If you want a devotional that will not flatter you, this is it.

Best for: Readers who appreciate conservative, holiness-focused, plain-spoken Bible teaching.

7. Jesus Calling: Sarah Young

Publisher: jesuscalling.com · First published: 2004

Sarah Young’s Jesus Calling has sold over 45 million copies and pioneered a very personal, first-person devotional style, written as though Jesus is speaking directly to the reader, with supporting Scripture references. Some readers find that style life-giving; others prefer their devotionals more expositional. Either way, it is impossible to ignore the comfort and intimacy with Christ this little book has brought to so many.

Best for: Readers in seasons of anxiety, grief or burnout who need a tender daily reminder of God’s presence.

8. In Touch Daily Devotional: Dr. Charles Stanley

Publisher: In Touch Ministries

Drawn from decades of Dr. Charles Stanley’s teaching ministry, In Touch is a beautifully produced monthly devotional with daily Scripture readings, a one-year Bible reading plan, and clear, pastoral reflections. The print magazine ships internationally, and the daily devotional is also available free by email, podcast and on intouch.org.

Best for: Readers who want pastoral, evangelical Bible teaching with a steady, fatherly tone.

9. The Word for Today: Bob & Debby Gass

Publisher: United Christian Broadcasters (UCB)

Launched in 1994 by the late Bob Gass, The Word for Today is now distributed by UCB to more than 3.5 million readers a quarter around the world, with editions for the UK, Asia Pacific and beyond. The style is short, punchy and intensely practical, perfect if you have only three minutes before you dash out the door. It is also one of the most accessible devotionals for new believers and seekers.

Best for: Busy readers who want bite-size, practical encouragement rooted in Scripture.

10. Streams in the Desert: L. B. Cowman

First published: 1925

Lettie B. Cowman wrote Streams in the Desert in the long, painful years of her husband’s illness on the mission field, weaving Scripture together with poetry and quotations from godly writers. A century later, this devotional is still in print, still being passed from hand to hand, still meeting people in their hardest seasons. If you are walking through suffering, this one will feel like it was written for you.

Best for: Anyone in a season of grief, waiting, or wilderness.

11. Starting Your Day Right: Joyce Meyer

Publisher: Joyce Meyer Ministries

Joyce Meyer’s Starting Your Day Right (and the free daily devotionals on joycemeyer.org) bring her trademark plain-spoken, no-nonsense approach to walking with God. Each entry is short, application-driven, and aimed squarely at how you actually live, feel and think today. Particularly strong on mindset, emotions and overcoming everyday struggles.

Best for: Readers who need practical, mindset-renewing encouragement to face the day.

12. Today’s Word: Joel & Victoria Osteen

Publisher: Joel Osteen Ministries

Joel and Victoria Osteen’s Today’s Word (the daily companion to their Hope for Today resources) is a short Scripture, a brief encouragement, and a prayer. It is upbeat, hope-focused and easy to read. Pair it with a more expositional devotional for a balanced diet.

Best for: Readers who need a daily lift of hope and encouragement.

13. Billy Graham Daily Devotional

Publisher: Billy Graham Evangelistic Association

Drawn from the writings and sermons of Billy Graham, arguably the most influential evangelist of the 20th century, the BGEA’s daily devotional pairs Scripture with Graham’s clear, gospel-centred reflections on topics like love, fear, loneliness, joy and hope. Free by email and on the BGEA website.

Best for: Readers who love classic evangelistic preaching and clear gospel application.

14. Morning and Evening: Charles H. Spurgeon

First published: 1869 · Read free: Christian Classics Ethereal Library

The “Prince of Preachers” gives you two short Scripture meditations a day, one for the morning and one for the evening, for all 365 days. Spurgeon’s writing is rich, Christ-exalting and unforgettable. Updated editions (such as Alistair Begg’s) make the language accessible for modern readers without losing his fire.

Best for: Readers who want depth, beauty and a strong Reformed flavour in their daily reading.

Bonus: YouVersion Bible App Plans

Publisher: YouVersion / Bible.com

Not a single devotional but a whole ecosystem. The free YouVersion Bible App offers thousands of devotional and reading plans, including many of the ones above, in dozens of languages, with audio, reminders and group features. If you want to sample five of the best daily devotionals in a month to find the one that fits you, this is the easiest way to do it.

How to Choose the Right Daily Devotional for You

With so many best daily devotionals available, the trick is not finding one, it is finding yours. A few questions to ask:

How much time do you actually have? Be honest. If five minutes is your real number, do not subscribe to a 30-minute devotional, you will quit by week three. The Gospel For Today, The Word for Today and Today’s Word are great in that range. If you have 20 minutes, Our Daily Bread, In Touch or Morning and Evening will reward you.

What season are you in? Suffering? Reach for Streams in the Desert. Drifting? Reach for My Utmost for His Highest. New to the faith? Start with Our Daily Bread or a YouVersion starter plan. Anxious? Jesus Calling meets you tenderly.

What tradition are you in? Your devotional diet should stretch you, but it should also feed you in your own language of faith. Pentecostal and charismatic readers will resonate strongly with Open Heavens, Rhapsody of Realities and Joyce Meyer. Reformed and evangelical readers will love Spurgeon, Chambers and In Touch. African readers will find home in Open Heavens, Rhapsody, Daily Manna and our own The Gospel For Today.

Pair short with long. Many of our editors use one quick devotional in the morning (for momentum) and one richer one in the evening (for depth). Try The Gospel For Today at breakfast and Spurgeon’s Morning and Evening at night, for example.

Start Tomorrow Morning With One of the Best Daily Devotionals

The real secret of every faithful Christian you admire is not that they found a magical devotional, it is that they showed up tomorrow morning, and the morning after that, and the one after that. Pick one or two of these best daily devotionals from this list, set a real time on your calendar, and start.

If you would like a short, faithful, Christ-centred Scripture meditation waiting in your morning, we would love to walk that road with you. Read today’s edition of The Gospel For Today on Gospelbuzz, bookmark the page, and make it part of your daily rhythm. And if your favourite among the best daily devotionals didn’t make our list, drop it in the comments, we read every one.

May your time in the Word tomorrow morning be the best five minutes of your day.
